newsitem.title: POLAND: Optimus to take 15 pct of Netia Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Optimus to take 15 pct of Netia Telecom.

text.p: Polish computer firm Optimus SA will take up to 14.9 percent in Netia Telecom SA, a consortium of international and Polish firms, in exchange for 75 percent of an Optimus subsidiary, a financial adviser to Optimus said.

Stefan Mroczek said told Reuters on Tuesday that Netia would take 75 percent in Optimus Invest SA, giving the two firms joint ownership in the telecom operator Polskie Telmedia, currently wholly-owned by Optimus Invest.
"Optimus is gaining the possiblity to hold up to 14.9 percent of Netia while we're providing Netia with 75 percent of the shares in Optimus Invest," Stefan Mroczek told Reuters. @
Mroczek said the deal would give Optimus and Netia access to 15 local telephone markets.
Netia currently has a licence to operate a local telephone network in 11 of Poland's 49 provinces while Polskie Telmedia has a licence to operate in four.
Mroczek also said it was possible that Optimus would later sell all its shares in Optimus Invest.
Netia's main shareholder with a 65-percent stake is RP Telekom company, which groups about 240 Polish and foreign firms including Israel's Dankner Group and Goldman Sachs investment bank.
Swedish Telia AB holds 25 percent and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) 10 percent.
